correctness.rationale: The count-vector chain has 12 transient states. The supplied table of twelve degree-four harmonic numerators and common denominator D(gamma) satisfies all generator Dirichlet equations; reconstructed all rates from ordered focal/speaker interactions independently and evaluated each degree<=5 polynomial residual at seven distinct exact rational gamma values, certifying the polynomial identities. For gamma>0 every transient state admits a positive-rate path to consensus, so the finite Dirichlet solution is unique. The displayed F(gamma) has positive majority gain for 0<gamma<1, equals 2/3 at gamma=1, and approaches 787/1131 as gamma decreases to zero. The derivative numerator has positive coefficients so F is strictly decreasing.

evidence: The ordinary voter model gamma=1 gives 2/3 via opinion-frequency martingale; the bi-layer primary paper treats larger-scale mean-field behavior.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A mean-field phase diagram and the gamma=1 martingale do not determine the finite n=3 mixed-channel hitting law for 0<gamma<1.

value.rationale: This is the smallest nontrivial two-versus-one majority setting in which symmetric microscopic tolerance rules give a strictly amplified consensus advantage. Exact rational dependence and a strictly monotone gain provide a motivated finite-mechanism counterexample to neutral initial-frequency intuition, despite the narrow n=3 scope.

limitations: The original paper allows update conventions beyond the explicitly fixed independent-clock model.
No claim for n>3, heterogeneous clocks or gamma=0 absorption.
